title: Fund in vitro fertilisation from the state budget
description: Item 1 of the Civic Coalition's '100 konkretów na pierwsze 100 dni' (100 concrete pledges for the first 100 days), presented at the KO convention in Tarnów: 'Wprowadzenie finansowania in vitro z budżetu państwa' (introduce state-budget funding for in vitro).
reasoning: The law obliges the health minister to spend at least 500 million PLN a year from the state budget on infertility treatment, and the national programme covering in vitro started on 1 June 2024, running to the end of 2028. The Ministry of Health reports more than 18,000 children born under the programme as of 31 August 2026. The pledge was delivered, about five and a half months after the government took office rather than within 100 days.
key_evidence: State programme 'Leczenie niepłodności obejmujące procedury medycznie wspomaganej prokreacji 2024–2028' in force since 1 June 2024
Statutory minimum of 500 million PLN per year from the state budget (about 2.5 billion PLN over 2024–2028)
Ministry of Health data as of 31 August 2026: 56,236 couples qualified, 34,622 clinical pregnancies, 18,040 children born

title: 1,500 PLN a month 'babciowe' for mothers returning to work
description: 100 konkretów pledge: 'Program "Aktywna mama" – 1500 zł miesięcznie za opiekę nad dzieckiem, tzw. babciowe', a monthly childcare benefit of 1,500 PLN for women returning to work after childbirth, usable e.g. to pay a grandparent or nanny.
reasoning: The 'Aktywny rodzic' (Active Parent) law, signed by President Andrzej Duda in June 2024, introduced from 1 October 2024 a 1,500 PLN monthly benefit ('aktywni rodzice w pracy', popularly 'babciowe') for working parents of children aged 12 to 35 months, paid by ZUS for up to 24 months, alongside daycare and stay-at-home variants. The benefit was opened to both working parents rather than only mothers and arrived later than the 100-day horizon; the fact-checker Demagog rates it as delivered with delay.
key_evidence: 'Aktywny rodzic' law of 15 May 2024, signed by the President (announced 10 June 2024)
1,500 PLN a month (1,900 PLN for children with disabilities) for 24 months, from the 12th to the 35th month of the child's life
Applications to ZUS opened on 1 October 2024
Demagog (two-year review): 'zrealizowane z opóźnieniem' (delivered with delay)

title: Raise teachers' pay by at least 30% (no less than 1,500 PLN gross)
description: 100 konkretów pledge: 'Podniesienie wynagrodzenia nauczycieli o co najmniej 30 proc. – nie mniej niż 1500 zł brutto podwyżki' (raise teachers' salaries by at least 30%, with a rise of no less than 1,500 PLN gross).
reasoning: The 2024 budget raised teachers' minimum base salaries retroactively from 1 January 2024 by 30% for appointed and chartered teachers and 33% for beginning teachers, meeting the percentage part of the pledge. The resulting increases in the minimum base salary (about 1,167–1,365 PLN gross for teachers with a master's degree) were below the promised floor of 1,500 PLN, which is why Demagog rates the pledge as only partially delivered. As of October 2026 it is recorded as delivered in a reduced form.
key_evidence: Minimum base pay 2023 → 2024 (master's degree, teaching qualification): beginning 3,690 → 4,908 PLN (+33%), appointed 3,890 → 5,057 PLN (+30%), chartered 4,550 → 5,915 PLN (+30%)
Rises applied from 1 January 2024 under the 2024 budget act and accompanying legislation
Demagog (two-year review): '1500 zł podwyżki dla nauczycieli' rated partially delivered

title: Legal abortion up to the 12th week of pregnancy
description: 100 konkretów pledge: 'Legalna, bezpieczna i dostępna aborcja do 12. tygodnia ciąży' (legal, safe and accessible abortion up to the 12th week). Tusk had pledged in June 2022 to 'guarantee it 100%'.
reasoning: Four bills to soften the abortion law passed first reading in April 2024, but on 12 July 2024 the Sejm rejected even the narrowest one (decriminalising assistance in abortion up to 12 weeks) by 218 to 215, with most PSL coalition MPs voting against. Tusk acknowledged in 2024 that reform was unlikely in this parliamentary term, and President Karol Nawrocki (in office since August 2025) supports the existing near-total ban. As of October 2026 the law has not changed and enactment within the term is not realistic; the government relied instead on guidance to hospitals within existing law.
key_evidence: 12 April 2024: Sejm sends four abortion bills to committee
12 July 2024: Sejm rejects the Left's decriminalisation bill 215–218 after a split in the ruling coalition
Tusk acknowledged in 2024 that abortion reform was unlikely during the current term (Notes from Poland, April 2026)
President Nawrocki supports the 2021 near-total ban; no liberalising law enacted as of October 2026

title: Introduce civil partnerships, including for same-sex couples
description: In August 2021, at the Campus Polska youth forum, Tusk said introducing civil partnerships would be 'one of my first decisions' if he led a parliamentary majority after the next elections; he repeated the pledge in June 2022. The government later pursued it through a narrower bill on the 'status osoby najbliższej' (closest-person status).
reasoning: A government civil-partnership bill presented in October 2024 stalled in consultation amid opposition from coalition partner PSL. A narrower government bill creating a notarised 'closest person' agreement, open to two adults of any sex, passed both chambers of parliament, but President Karol Nawrocki vetoed it in mid-July 2026 citing the constitutional protection of marriage, and on 17 September 2026 the Sejm failed to override the veto (232 for, 259 needed). As of October 2026 no partnership law is in force and enactment before the end of the term looks unlikely; the verdict reflects the outcome, as the government did pursue the measure.
key_evidence: August 2021: Tusk says civil partnerships would be 'one of my first decisions' in power
October 2024: government bill presented; June 2025 still in consultation awaiting the PM's approval
'Status osoby najbliższej' bill and implementing bill passed by both chambers; vetoed by President Nawrocki in mid-July 2026
17 September 2026: veto override fails in the Sejm, 232 for and 199 against with 259 votes required

title: Separate the offices of Minister of Justice and Prosecutor General
description: 100 konkretów pledge (rule-of-law section): 'Rozdzielenie funkcji ministra sprawiedliwości i prokuratora generalnego', ending the 2016 arrangement under which the justice minister also serves as Prosecutor General.
reasoning: As of October 2026 the two offices remain combined. A government bill (UD95, Minister of Justice Waldemar Żurek) on the government's legislative list would create a Prosecutor General separate from the minister, elected by the Sejm with Senate consent for a single six-year term, with adoption by the Council of Ministers planned for Q3 2026; no adoption had been found at the research date. On 15 September 2026 the ministry's codification commission handed over a full draft of a new law on the prosecution service built on the same separation.
key_evidence: Government legislative list: draft UD95 amending the Law on the Prosecution Service, Prosecutor General 'nie będzie złączony z funkcją Ministra Sprawiedliwości', planned adoption Q3 2026
15 September 2026: Codification Commission on the Judiciary and Prosecution delivers a draft 'Prawo o ustroju Prokuratury' to the Ministry of Justice
Demagog (two-year review): rated partially delivered
No separation law passed by the Sejm as of October 2026

title: Unblock EU funds frozen over rule-of-law disputes
description: 100 konkretów pledge: 'Uzyskanie pieniędzy z funduszy unijnych' (obtain the EU money), referring chiefly to the Recovery and Resilience Facility (KPO) and cohesion funds withheld under the previous government over judicial-independence concerns.
reasoning: On 29 February 2024 the European Commission adopted two decisions opening Poland's access to up to EUR 137 billion: a positive preliminary assessment of the first recovery-plan payment request (EUR 6.3 billion) and confirmation that Poland met the Charter-related enabling condition for up to EUR 76.5 billion of cohesion funds. Poland also joined the European Public Prosecutor's Office. Access to the funds was restored; how much has actually been disbursed and spent is a separate question, as press reviews in October 2026 note.
key_evidence: European Commission press release IP/24/1222 (29 February 2024): path to up to EUR 137 billion in EU funds
Up to EUR 59.8 billion under the Recovery and Resilience Facility (EUR 25.3 bn grants, EUR 34.5 bn loans) through 2026
Demagog (two-year review): rated delivered

title: Return to a flat-rate health contribution for entrepreneurs
description: 100 konkretów pledge: 'Powrót do ryczałtowego systemu rozliczania składki zdrowotnej', undoing the income-linked health contribution for the self-employed introduced by the PiS government's 'Polski Ład' in 2022.
reasoning: Only limited relief has taken effect: from 1 January 2025 the minimum contribution base was temporarily lowered to 75% of the minimum wage and sales of fixed assets were excluded from the base. The main reform, a two-part contribution passed by the Sejm on 4 April 2025, was vetoed by President Andrzej Duda on 6 May 2025, and in 2026 the minimum base returned to 100% of the minimum wage. As of October 2026 there is no flat-rate system; the fact-checker Demagog and a Fakt/Super Biznes review rate the pledge as partially delivered, though the delivered part is small relative to the promise.
key_evidence: Since 1 January 2025: fixed-asset sales excluded from the health-contribution base; 2025 minimum base reduced to 75% of the minimum wage
4 April 2025: Sejm passes a bill lowering the health contribution from 2026 (two-part flat plus percentage contribution)
6 May 2025: President Duda vetoes the bill
2026: minimum base back at 100% of the minimum wage; no new reform enacted as of October 2026

title: 0% interest loan for buying a first home
description: 100 konkretów pledge: 'Kredyt z oprocentowaniem 0 proc. na zakup pierwszego mieszkania' (a zero-interest mortgage for first-time buyers), later developed as the '#naStart' programme.
reasoning: The programme was contested, including by coalition partner Poland 2050's leader Szymon Hołownia, over its likely effect on house prices. In December 2024 the Minister of Development and Technology, Krzysztof Paszyk, announced that the government would not introduce the 0% loan and would present a different housing programme instead. As of October 2026 the scheme has never been launched.
key_evidence: 12–13 December 2024: Minister Krzysztof Paszyk says on Radio Zet 'Nie będzie kredytu 0 proc.'
Government said a new housing programme would be presented instead
October 2026 review: the '#naStart' 0% loan 'ostatecznie nie został uruchomiony' (was ultimately never launched)

title: Double the income-tax-free allowance to 60,000 PLN
description: 100 konkretów pledge: 'Podniesienie kwoty wolnej od podatku – z 30 tys. zł do 60 tys. zł' (raise the personal income tax-free amount from 30,000 to 60,000 PLN).
reasoning: As of October 2026 the tax-free amount is still 30,000 PLN. On 19 August 2026 Tusk said the government was not formally abandoning the pledge but that it would 'certainly not be possible within a year and a half' and was unrealistic in 2027 and 2028, citing defence spending; the Finance Ministry costs it at 58.6 billion PLN a year. The government instead proposed raising the first PIT bracket from 120,000 to 130,000 PLN with a new 24% rate (adopted as a draft on 29 September 2026). Because the Sejm's term ends in autumn 2027, the pledge cannot be delivered within this term.
key_evidence: Kwota wolna remains at 30,000 PLN in 2026
19 August 2026, Tusk: raising it is 'mało realna' in 2027 and 2028 and 'na pewno w perspektywie półtora roku nie będzie możliwe'
Finance Ministry estimate: 58.6 billion PLN a year
Alternative plan: 12% up to 130,000 PLN, 24% from 130,000 to 150,000 PLN, 32% above (government draft, September 2026)

title: Exempt savings and investments up to 100,000 PLN from the 'Belka' capital-gains tax
description: 100 konkretów pledge: 'Złożenie propozycji zniesienia podatku od zysków kapitałowych (podatek Belki)' for savings and investments, including on the Warsaw Stock Exchange, of up to 100,000 PLN held for more than a year.
reasoning: The pledge was delivered late and in altered form through Personal Investment Accounts (Osobiste Konta Inwestycyjne, OKI). The Sejm passed the law on 3 July 2026 (427 for, 5 against), and President Nawrocki signed it on 13 August 2026; it takes effect on 1 January 2027. Investment assets up to 100,000 PLN are exempt from the 19% Belka tax, but deposits and bonds are capped at 25,000 PLN within that limit, and assets above the caps face a new annual tax on their value of up to about 1% (0.85% in 2027).
key_evidence: OKI law passed by the Sejm on 3 July 2026 (427–5–1); signed by President Nawrocki on 13 August 2026
In force from 1 January 2027; limits indexed to inflation from 2030
Exemption: investment assets up to 100,000 PLN; savings component (deposits, bonds) capped at 25,000 PLN
New tax on the value of assets above the limits, at most about 1% according to the government

title: 'Leave for entrepreneurs': one month a year without social-insurance contributions
description: 100 konkretów pledge: 'Urlop dla przedsiębiorców', one month a year without paying social-insurance (ZUS) contributions, together with a leave benefit of half the minimum wage.
reasoning: The 'wakacje składkowe' (ZUS contribution holiday) has applied since November 2024: eligible micro-entrepreneurs can skip their own social-insurance contributions for one month a year, with the state budget covering them. The promised leave benefit of half the minimum wage was not introduced, which is why Demagog rates the pledge as partially delivered. As of October 2026 the core relief is in force in a narrower form than promised.
key_evidence: Contribution holiday available since November 2024 for micro-entrepreneurs, one month per year
Covers the entrepreneur's own social-insurance contributions only
No leave benefit of half the minimum wage introduced
Demagog (two-year review): 'urlop dla przedsiębiorców' rated partially delivered
